sections.title: Samuel
sections.description: Samuel's birth, calling, and service as judge

sections.title: Saul
sections.description: Israel's first king and his downfall

sections.title: David's Path to the Throne
sections.description: David is anointed, flees from Saul, and Saul dies

events.title: Hannah's Prayer and Samuel's Birth
events.description: Hannah is barren and prays earnestly to the Lord in the tabernacle at Shiloh. She vows that if she has a son, he will be dedicated to the Lord for his entire life. The Lord hears her prayer, and she gives birth to a son whom she names Samuel, because "I have asked him of the Lord."

events.title: Samuel Dedicated to the Lord
events.description: When Samuel is weaned, Hannah takes him to the house of the Lord in Shiloh and entrusts him to the priest Eli. She brings an offering and sings a song of praise to the Lord that celebrates His power and justice. Samuel stays with Eli and serves before the Lord.

events.title: The Lord Calls Samuel
events.description: The Lord calls out to the young Samuel during the night while he is lying in the temple. Three times Samuel thinks it is Eli calling, but Eli finally realizes it is the Lord. Samuel receives a solemn message about judgment on Eli's house. All Israel comes to know that Samuel is established as the Lord's prophet.

events.title: The Ark of the Covenant Taken by the Philistines
events.description: Israel goes to war against the Philistines and suffers defeat. They bring the Ark of the Covenant from Shiloh to secure victory, but the Philistines defeat them again and capture the ark. Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, die in battle. When Eli hears the news, he falls from his chair and breaks his neck.

events.title: The Ark Returned to Israel
events.description: The Ark of the Covenant brings plagues upon the Philistines. The idol Dagon falls before the ark, and the cities are struck with tumors. After seven months, the Philistines send the ark back on a cart pulled by two cows, along with gold objects as a guilt offering. The ark arrives at Beth-Shemesh and then at Kiriath-Jearim.

events.title: Victory at Mizpah
events.description: Samuel gathers all Israel at Mizpah to seek the Lord. The people fast and confess their sins. When the Philistines attack, Samuel cries out to the Lord, and the Lord sends a mighty thunderstorm that throws the Philistines into confusion. Israel pursues them and wins a great victory. Samuel sets up a stone and calls it Ebenezer.

events.title: The People Demand a King
events.description: When Samuel grows old, he appoints his sons as judges, but they are corrupt. The elders of Israel come to Samuel and demand a king "like all the other nations." Samuel warns them about what a king will require of them, but the people insist. The Lord tells Samuel that they have not rejected him, but God himself as their king.

events.title: Saul Anointed as King
events.description: Saul, son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin, is out looking for his father's lost donkeys when he meets Samuel. The Lord has already revealed to Samuel that this man will be anointed prince over Israel. Samuel secretly anoints Saul and gives him signs confirming his calling. The Spirit of the Lord comes upon Saul, and he prophesies among the prophets.

events.title: Saul Confirmed as King
events.description: Samuel gathers the people at Mizpah to choose a king by lot. The lot falls on Saul, but he has hidden himself among the baggage. They find him and bring him forward. Samuel declares: "See the one the Lord has chosen!" The people shout: "Long live the king!" Later, Saul confirms his leadership by defeating the Ammonites who are besieging Jabesh in Gilead.

events.title: Saul's Disobedience at the Sacrifice
events.description: The Philistines gather a mighty army against Israel. Saul waits for Samuel at Gilgal, but when Samuel does not arrive at the appointed time and the soldiers begin to desert, Saul offers the burnt offering himself. Samuel arrives shortly after and rebukes him: his kingdom will not endure because he did not keep the Lord's command.

events.title: Jonathan Attacks the Philistines
events.description: Jonathan and his armor-bearer sneak up to the Philistine outpost at Michmash. They trust in the Lord and kill about twenty men. The Lord sends panic into the Philistine camp, and the earth trembles. Saul and the rest of the army join the pursuit. Saul places the people under a foolish oath to fast, which nearly costs Jonathan his life.

events.title: Saul Rejected - The War Against Amalek
events.description: The Lord commands Saul through Samuel to completely destroy the Amalekites. Saul wins the battle but spares King Agag and the best of the livestock. Samuel confronts him: "Obedience is better than sacrifice." Samuel proclaims that the Lord has rejected Saul as king over Israel. Samuel himself cuts down Agag before the Lord in Gilgal.

events.title: David Anointed as King
events.description: The Lord sends Samuel to Jesse in Bethlehem to anoint a new king. Samuel sees Jesse's sons one by one, but the Lord chooses none of them. Finally, they bring the youngest, David, who is tending sheep. The Lord says: "Rise and anoint him, for this is he." Samuel anoints David, and the Spirit of the Lord comes powerfully upon him from that day forward.

events.title: David and Goliath
events.description: The Philistine giant Goliath from Gath challenges Israel to single combat for forty days, but no one dares to face him. The young David comes with food for his brothers and hears the challenge. He refuses Saul's armor and goes against the giant with a sling and five stones. David strikes Goliath in the forehead, and the giant falls. David cuts off his head with his own sword.

events.title: David and Jonathan's Friendship
events.description: After the victory over Goliath, Jonathan, Saul's son, forms a deep bond of friendship with David. Jonathan gives David his own robe, armor, and weapons as a sign of their covenant. The women sing that "Saul has slain his thousands, but David his tens of thousands," and Saul becomes jealous and begins to fear David.

events.title: Saul Hunts David
events.description: Saul's jealousy grows into murder plots. He throws his spear at David twice. David marries Saul's daughter Michal after killing two hundred Philistines. Saul orders Jonathan and his servants to kill David, but Jonathan intervenes. Michal helps David escape through a window. David seeks refuge with Samuel in Ramah.

events.title: David at Ahimelech in Nob
events.description: David flees to the priest Ahimelech in Nob and pretends he is on a mission for the king. He receives the bread of the Presence to eat and takes Goliath's sword. Then he flees to King Achish in Gath, but becomes afraid and pretends to be mad to escape.

events.title: David in the Wilderness
events.description: David gathers a group of about four hundred men around him in the cave of Adullam. He takes his parents to safety in Moab. David saves the city of Keilah from the Philistines, but must flee again when Saul arrives. In the wilderness of Ziph, the inhabitants try to betray David to Saul, but David escapes time and again.

events.title: David Spares Saul's Life in the Cave
events.description: Saul enters a cave at En-Gedi to relieve himself, unaware that David and his men are hiding deep inside. David sneaks up and cuts off a corner of Saul's robe. Afterwards, he calls out to Saul and shows the piece of cloth as proof that he means no harm. Saul weeps and admits that David is more righteous than he.

events.title: Nabal and Abigail
events.description: David sends messengers to the wealthy Nabal, requesting supplies in gratitude for his men's protection of Nabal's shepherds. Nabal rebuffs them with contempt. David sets out with four hundred men to take revenge. Nabal's wise wife, Abigail, meets David with generous gifts and persuades him to spare his anger. David blesses her for preventing bloodshed. Ten days later, the Lord strikes Nabal, and David takes Abigail as his wife.

events.title: David Spares Saul's Life in the Camp
events.description: The Ziphites betray David again. David and Abishai sneak into Saul's camp at night while everyone is in a deep sleep sent by the Lord. Abishai wants to kill Saul, but David forbids it: "Who can lay hands on the Lord's anointed and remain guiltless?" David takes Saul's spear and water jug, then calls out to Abner from a distance. Saul once again acknowledges his sin.

events.title: David Among the Philistines
events.description: David loses hope of surviving Saul in Israel and flees to King Achish of Gath with his six hundred men. Achish gives him the town of Ziklag. David lives in Philistine territory for a year and four months, raiding neighboring lands while making Achish believe he is attacking Judah.

events.title: Saul and the Medium at En-Dor
events.description: The Philistines gather for war. Saul is afraid and seeks an answer from the Lord, but the Lord does not reply to him through dreams, Urim, or prophets. In desperation, Saul visits a medium at En-Dor and asks her to summon Samuel's spirit. Samuel tells Saul that the Lord has torn the kingdom from him and that he and his sons will die in tomorrow's battle.

events.title: The Philistines Refuse to Let David Fight
events.description: The Philistine commanders gather for war against Israel but object to David and his men marching with them, fearing he will turn against them in battle. Despite trusting him, King Achish sends David back to Ziklag.

events.title: David Retakes Ziklag
events.description: While David is away, the Amalekites raid Ziklag, burn the city, and take all the women and children captive, including David's two wives. David's men weep until they have no tears left, and some speak of stoning him. David strengthens himself in the Lord his God, seeks guidance from the Lord through the priest Abiathar, and pursues the Amalekites. He defeats them and rescues everyone.

events.title: The Death of Saul at Gilboa
events.description: The Philistines defeat Israel on Mount Gilboa. Saul's three sons, Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malkishua, fall in battle. Saul is severely wounded by archers. To avoid being dishonored by the Philistines, he falls on his own sword. The Philistines find the dead bodies and hang them on the wall of Beth-shan. Brave men from Jabesh-gilead retrieve the bodies and bury them.
